title: Deadlock when using SseBroadcasterImpl
body:
### Describe the bug

I am currently using quarkus 3.29.2 but I am facing this issue for quite a while now since we added SSE endpionts to our application. This is already a couple of major quarkus versions ago.

The issue is that once in a while the sending of SSE events to registered clients stopps and the vert.x BlockedThreadChecker warns me about threads that have been blocked.

> WARN  [io.ve.co.im.BlockedThreadChecker] (vertx-blocked-thread-checker) Thread Thread[vert.x-eventloop-thread-44,5,main] has been blocked for XXXX ms, time limit is 2000 ms {} : io.vertx.core.VertxException: Thread blocked

Now I was finally able to track down the issue to a deadlock scenario that occurs between the **SseBroadcasterImpl** and the **SseEventSinkImpl** when a new SSE-Event is sent to the SseEventSink while at the same time it is beeing closed in a different thread.

```
Found one Java-level deadlock:
=============================
"vert.x-eventloop-thread-26":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fd40800fe40 (object 0x0000000614490518, a org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.server.jaxrs.SseBroadcasterImpl),
  which is held by "NotificationReceiver Thread"

"NotificationReceiver Thread":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fd3d8371d00 (object 0x00000006154fe248, a org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.server.jaxrs.SseEventSinkImpl),
  which is held by "vert.x-eventloop-thread-44"

"vert.x-eventloop-thread-44":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fd40800fe40 (object 0x0000000614490518, a org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.server.jaxrs.SseBroadcasterImpl),
  which is held by "NotificationReceiver Thread"

```
I believe what happens here is as follows:

A SseEventSinkImpl instance will be registered on a SseBroadcasterImpl instance when the client calls the SSE endpoint. During registration the SseEventSink remembers the instance of  the SseBroadcaster
```
void register(SseBroadcasterImpl broadcaster) {
        if (this.broadcaster != null)
            throw new IllegalStateException("Already registered on a broadcaster");
        this.broadcaster = broadcaster;
}
```
When the SseEventSink gets closed after a while, the broadcaster reference is used to signal the broadcaster that this instance was closed and should be removed.
```
public synchronized void close() {
        .....................
        if (broadcaster != null)
            broadcaster.fireClose(this);
    }
```
The broadcaster.fireClose() method is also synchronized on a method level
```
synchronized void fireClose(SseEventSinkImpl sseEventSink)
```

Now, when at the same time as the SseEventSink is getting closed in one thread and another thread tries to send an event into the sink via the synchronized SseBreadcaster.broadcast() method, every registered SseEventSink is called and its send() method gets invoked.
```
public synchronized CompletionStage<?> broadcast(OutboundSseEvent event) {
        for (int i = 0; i < sinks.size(); i++) {
           SseEventSink sseEventSink = sinks.get(i);
           try {
                cs = sseEventSink.send(event).exceptionally((t) -> {
                    .......
                });
            } catch (Exception e) {
              .....
            }
            .....
        }
        .....
}
```
The SseEventSink.send() method itself is not synchronizen, but is calls the synchronized `isClosed(`) method
```
public synchronized boolean isClosed() {
        return context.serverResponse().closed() || closed;
}
```
And this is where the cycle gets closed and the dead lock is created. I will attach the complete thread dump of the threads in question as attachment where you can see the exact line numbers.

If I understand the whole szenario correctly than the issue is that we have a circular relationship between the one SseBroadcaster instance that manages multiple SseEventSink instances. By chance the `close()` method on one of the SseEventSink instances calls the `broadcaster.fireClose()` method at the same time as the `SseBroadcaster.broadcast()` method tries to call `SseEventSink.send()` on the same instance. Because all of the methods are synchronized but get called in reverse order a dead-lock is the result.

Thread1: `sseEventSink.close() [synchronized] -> broadcaster.fireClose() [synchronized]`
Thread2: `broadcaster.broadcast() [synchronized] -> sseEventSink.send() -> sseEventSink.isCLosed() [synchronized]`

I hope this is not to confusing to understand but I think the attached thread dumps should help. There is also a chance that my implementation is doing something odd but it is quite straight forward. When the client calls the endpoint than `broadcaster.register(sseEventSink)` is called in order to register the new client on the broadcaster. The events will be broadcasted from an event handling thread with `broadcaster.broadcast(sseEvent)`.

### Expected behavior

No deadlock between threads

### Actual behavior

> Found one Java-level deadlock:
=============================
"vert.x-eventloop-thread-26":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fd40800fe40 (object 0x0000000614490518, a org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.server.jaxrs.SseBroadcasterImpl),
  which is held by "NotificationReceiver Thread"

"NotificationReceiver Thread":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fd3d8371d00 (object 0x00000006154fe248, a org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.server.jaxrs.SseEventSinkImpl),
  which is held by "vert.x-eventloop-thread-44"

"vert.x-eventloop-thread-44":
  waiting to lock monitor 0x00007fd40800fe40 (object 0x0000000614490518, a org.jboss.resteasy.reactive.server.jaxrs.SseBroadcasterImpl),
  which is held by "NotificationReceiver Thread"

### How to Reproduce?

Unfortunately I was not able to manually reproduce this behaviour because it requires a very special order of concurrent actions being executed at the same time. 
I faced this issue at least 4 times in the last 12 weeks in our application and was now finally able to hunt it down. 
A restart of the quarkus process could solved the issue.

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

4.18.0-553.76.1.el8_10.x86_64

### Output of `java -version`

OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (Red_Hat-21.0.8.0.9-1)

### Quarkus version or git rev

3.29.2

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

gradle 9.2.0
